name: Green Phoenix-ShopPOS
tagline: A staff-only point-of-sale and cash-drawer tool built for one independent auto repair shop.
platforms: iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android, web portal
status: Private beta (TestFlight, internal testers), for one shop
about:
Green Phoenix-ShopPOS is an internal tool for one auto repair shop. The shop's staff use it to ring up payments against repair orders, count the cash drawer, track parts and see the day's takings. It is not a consumer app and it is not for the public: you need a staff sign-in from the shop, and it only works with the shop's own server.

The people whose information it holds are the shop's customers (name, vehicle, payments) and the shop's employees (sign-in and activity). Customers do not use the app and have no accounts. All of this data is kept on the shop's own server at the shop, not in a cloud service run by the developer. The app is pre-pointed at that server. It is currently shared only with named testers through TestFlight and has not been released on the App Store.

collects.why: Look up what a repair order owes so it can be paid and reconciled

collects.why: Record part costs against repair orders

collects.what: Vehicle license plate and VIN seen on a repair order
collects.why: Find a repair order by plate or VIN

collects.what: Payments: method (cash, credit, debit, check, store credit), amount, cash handed over and change, card brand, the last 4 digits of a card only, a terminal approval reference, and check number
collects.why: The shop's record of money taken

collects.why: Let staff sign in and show who did what

collects.what: Staff pay rates (visible to admins only)
An audit trail of who did what and when (every sale, drawer action and override), with the device used
Staff tasks and staff-written receipt notes
Device list (device label, kind, last seen), push-notification tokens, and, for the optional Live sales card, the tokens Apple gives the app to update that card

collects.why: Sign in without retyping the PIN

collects.shared: Sent only to the shop's own server

collects.why: Show current figures without opening the app, and answer Siri or Shortcuts questions

usage_data:
The apps and the web portal record what happens so problems can be found and fixed. Staff are told the apps record their activity.

The iPhone, iPad and Mac app writes a heartbeat line every 10 seconds, even when idle. It says which screen is showing, whether the app is idle or busy, whether the person is signed in, whether it is offline, how many sales are waiting, the network type, and memory, CPU, disk, battery and heat readings. The app also records taps and drags, and pointer movement on the Mac, plus each request to the server (the method, the path without any query, the result and the time). The heartbeat is uploaded to the shop's own server. The detailed tap, drag and pointer log stays on the device unless the person shares the logs or sends a problem report.

The web portal records a heartbeat every 10 seconds, every click (the control's name and the first 40 characters of its label), screen changes, calls to the server with their results and timings, mouse-pointer position about four times a second, scrolling, errors, and how many keys were typed in each field. It is designed not to record which keys were pressed. These records are uploaded to the shop's own server. The sign-in screen and number keypads are left out of the click and pointer trail.

The shop's server also keeps its own heartbeat and a log of every request, including who made it by name and the network address. The Android app shows the web portal inside the app, so it uploads the portal's activity records described above (clicks, pointer positions and key counts) to the shop's server as well.

The Help screen's self-checks run on the device (it uses Apple's on-device language model where available). Settings also has a passcode-protected developer log viewer for the developer's own use; it unlocks no extra features. Nothing is sent from Help unless the person taps Send to support.

PINs, passwords, tokens, keys, card numbers and device push tokens are designed not to be logged. Logs are tied to the signed-in person and the device. They are not sent to any analytics service.

Retention: logs on a device are kept for 30 days, with a size limit of about 1 GB. On the server, heartbeat, pointer and scroll records are kept for 30 days and other activity records for 90 days, then deleted automatically.
not_collected: No advertising and no ad networks
No tracking of people across other apps or websites, and no advertising identifier
No analytics, crash-reporting or tracking software added to the apps
No location, contacts, photo library, microphone, health or calendar access
No full card numbers are stored; only the last 4 digits, the card brand and an approval reference
The apps do not read or store card details themselves; they contain no card reader or payment software
No accounts with Google, Apple or any other third party, and no sign-in with them
Customers do not sign in and do not use the app

third_parties.what: Push tokens and the notification itself. Silent refresh notifications carry no data. Optional visible alerts for admins, each with its own switch, do carry details: a sale alert shows the amount, the repair-order number and the name of the staff member who rang it, and a pay-out alert shows the amount and who. These travel through Apple's push service. A duplicate-payment alert carries no figure. The optional Live sales card is updated by the server through Apple with the day's takings total in dollars. Siri requests are handled by Apple under Apple's own policies.

A browser add-on used by staff, the Helper, reads repair-order pages and sends that information to the shop's server. It also reads parts-order and invoice pages from parts vendors the person opens (AutoZone, O'Reilly, First Call, and Amazon and eBay order pages) to log part costs. When a person presses a write button, it writes payments, parts-received marks and inspection photos back into the shop's own account in that software.

The Helper posts shop alerts, such as inspection complete or authorized, to the shop's team chat channels. These messages include the repair-order number, the customer's name and the vehicle. The server also posts a nightly parts check there, and reads photos of invoices from one thread. Only people in the shop's team chat see these posts.

third_parties.who: A public message relay (for 'Can't reach the server' and Help reports)
third_parties.what: When a person taps 'Can't reach the server' or Help, then 'Send to support', a report is sent around the shop's server on purpose, because the server may be the thing that is down. It holds the app and version, the device model, the network type, the server's name and the addresses it looked up to, the error, the time, and an optional note (Help reports add the help chat and recent log lines, which the person sees first). It is encrypted so that only the developer can read it. The relay sees only the encrypted package and the sender's network address.

In the web portal and the Helper only, the report above looks up the shop server's name through Cloudflare's public name service. Cloudflare sees that server name. The apps use the device's own lookup.
Carries the traffic between staff devices and the shop's server. It is a connection service, not a place where data is kept; traffic to the shop's server is encrypted.

third_parties.who: iCloud Drive on the shop's Apple account (backups)
third_parties.what: Nightly backups of the shop server's database are copied there. These backups hold all of the data described on this page.

The developer uses an AI coding assistant with read-only access to the shop's reports, error alerts and problem reports to run audits and checks. This is the developer's own tooling and not a feature of the app.

permissions.name: Camera (iPhone and iPad)
permissions.why: To scan a receipt's barcode or a part's label to pull it up.

permissions.name: Face ID or Touch ID
permissions.why: Optional. To sign in without retyping your PIN.

permissions.name: Bluetooth
permissions.why: To print part labels on the shop's label maker.

permissions.name: Local network
permissions.why: To find the shop's server on the shop's network so setting up a phone or Mac takes one tap.

permissions.name: Notifications
permissions.why: Silent refreshes keep widgets current. Visible alerts are optional and for admins; sale and pay-out alerts show the amount (see above).

permissions.name: Siri and Shortcuts
permissions.why: Optional. To ask Siri or a Shortcut for sales, today's takings or a repair order. It answers from the shop's server with your own sign-in and permissions.

permissions.name: Live Activities (iPhone)
permissions.why: Optional. To show the day's takings, server status or offline state on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island. Admins can end it with the Stop Live Activity button in Settings.

permissions.name: Mac: network, Bluetooth, printing, files you choose
permissions.why: To reach the shop's server, use the label maker, print, and save or share exports.

retention:
On your device: in the app, go to Settings and choose Erase All Data on This Device. It removes the saved server, your sign-in and Face ID PIN, the cached price book, the offline log, waiting reports, app logs and settings, and then the app behaves like a fresh install. It is refused while offline sales are still waiting to upload. It does not touch anything on the shop's server, other devices or iCloud. Deleting the app also removes the data stored on that device.

On the shop's server: financial and audit records are kept as permanent records by design. Sales, payments, drawer and cash movements, store credit, the audit trail and problem reports can only be added to and cannot be edited or deleted; a correction is entered as a new reversing record. Staff accounts are deactivated, never deleted, so names keep showing correctly on past records. Activity logs are deleted automatically after 30 or 90 days as described above. Backup copies older than 60 days are removed, always keeping the newest 14.

The app has no self-service button for a customer or former employee to ask for their data to be deleted. Customers and staff can ask the shop about the information it holds, because the shop runs the server and holds the records. Because financial records are permanent by design, the shop may not be able to remove them.
children: Green Phoenix-ShopPOS is not directed at children. It is a staff-only work tool that needs a sign-in from the shop. It does not ask for anyone's age or birth date and has no features aimed at children.
support_what:
Green Phoenix-ShopPOS is the shop's own point-of-sale tool. Staff use it to ring up payments against repair orders, count the cash drawer, track parts and see the day's takings. It is made for one auto repair shop and works only with that shop's server.

It is a private beta shared through TestFlight with named testers. Everyone who uses it is staff at the shop.

If the internet is down but the shop's network is up, the app can keep working with the shop's server over the shop network.
support_steps: Install the app from the TestFlight invitation the shop gave you, or open the shop's web portal.
On first launch, follow the welcome and setup. The app looks for the shop's server on the shop's network, and you can change the server later in Settings.
Sign in with the PIN or password the shop gave you. You can turn on Face ID or Touch ID to skip retyping the PIN.
Ring up a payment by finding the repair order, or scan its receipt barcode on iPhone or iPad.
If something goes wrong, open the Help screen in the app and follow the self-checks.

support_faq.q: I can't sign in or I don't have access.
support_faq.a: Green Phoenix-ShopPOS is for the shop's staff only. Ask the shop's manager to give you access or reset your sign-in.

support_faq.q: The app says it can't reach the server.
support_faq.a: Check that you are connected to the internet or the shop's network. If the problem stays, tap the Can't reach the server button, which appears by itself when a request fails and is always in Settings. It sends a report straight to the developer without going through the shop's server.

support_faq.q: What happens if the internet drops while I'm ringing up a sale?
support_faq.a: The app keeps working from a saved copy of the price book and holds waiting sales on the device. They upload when the connection returns. Erase All Data is refused while sales are still waiting to upload.

support_faq.q: How do I use Face ID or Touch ID to sign in?
support_faq.a: It is optional and set per person. After you sign in with your PIN, you can choose to use Face ID or Touch ID next time. Your PIN is kept in your device's secure Keychain, on this device only.

support_faq.q: How do I clear everything the app saved on my device?
support_faq.a: Go to Settings and choose Erase All Data on This Device. It lists what will be removed and says clearly that nothing on the shop's server or other devices is touched.

support_faq.q: A customer asks what information the shop keeps about them.
support_faq.a: Customers should ask the shop. The shop holds the records on its own server, and financial records are kept as permanent records by design.
